lesson_title: How Coal Becomes Your Phone Charge
hook_text: Your phone charger is the last link in a chain that starts with a lump of coal — and before that, ancient sunlight.
clip_script: Step one: coal stores chemical potential energy, captured from sunlight by plants millions of years ago. Step two: it burns in a giant furnace, releasing heat. Step three: the heat boils water into high-pressure steam. Its particles are racing: kinetic energy. Step four: the steam slams into a turbine and spins it. Step five: the turbine turns a generator, and out comes electricity. Step six: wires carry it to your wall socket. But at every step, energy leaks away as heat, so only about a third of the coal's energy reaches the wires. Same story everywhere. A bicycle swaps speed for height on a hill. A cane cutter turns breakfast into a swinging arm. Stored energy, moving energy, always changing form.
visual_style: Whiteboard chain of six linked boxes from a lump of coal to a phone, with little heat squiggles escaping at every link; then quick cuts to a bicycle on a hill and a farm worker swinging a cane knife.
pacing: Six snappy steps, a punchy one-third fact, a fast montage finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace the energy through any system.
